$comment: Who reads Tenon. One route for all of them: a git dependency pinned to a tag. sync reports which tag each is on and writes nothing — bumping a consumer means editing its own package.json and reinstalling, which is the point of pinning. An earlier version of this file had a second 'vendor' route that copied the built CSS into to-dos, on the belief that to-dos had no npm. It has React 18, Vite and TypeScript at its root. Its built CSS is copied out of node_modules into kanban/dist/ by its own vite build, beside board-ui.js, because the Vercel deployment has no server and no node_modules and a static path is the only one both can reach. Two kinds of reader. The three below install the package at a tag and are what sync reports on. ai_chat_engine is the other kind: it is dropped into hosts it does not control, so it cannot require one to load a stylesheet first — every --aic-* default reads a --tenon- name with its old literal as the fallback, which needs nothing installed and is invisible to sync.
